purpose: Privacy-safe, repository-grounded verification ledger for the local Spec Kit integration. This file records evidence and limitations; it is not a release, merge, human-approval, or production attestation.

original_scope.requested_outcome: Install and fully integrate the latest stable official GitHub Spec Kit for Codex CLI into the existing repository without changing product code.
requirements: Inspect repository structure, applicable AGENTS.md files, instructions, skills, hooks, and Git state before mutation.
Use an isolated branch or control commit and preserve the original dirty checkout.
Verify the latest stable official github/spec-kit release, install Specify CLI through uv, and initialize in the existing repository root with Codex integration and the OS-appropriate script type.
Avoid blind overwrite, repository vendoring, and destructive reinitialization; use supported integration maintenance commands when a partial installation exists.
Verify .specify/ and .agents/skills/speckit-* and prove that Codex discovers the repository skills.
Confirm Codex is the active Spec Kit integration.

Create a project-grounded constitution that preserves production-data integrity and covers full feature lifecycle, UI/UX, states, errors, recovery, accessibility, cross-platform behavior, security, performance, testing, and factual verification.
Add AGENTS.md routing for compact local work, the full Spec Kit lifecycle for nontrivial work, and stronger review for high-risk work.
Review the final Git diff, conflicts, preservation of existing instructions, commands actually run, automatic behavior, and explicit commands.
non_goals: No production, deployment, store, customer-data, GitHub issue, commit, push, merge, or release side effects.
No claim of Windows, native-device, public-runtime, human-acceptance, or release verification.

finding_ledger.finding: The existing broad memory/ ignore rule could hide the constitution.
finding_ledger.resolution: Added narrow .specify/memory exceptions; negative controls confirm future unrelated memory remains ignored.

finding_ledger.finding: Spec Kit extension cache and bug working records are runtime artifacts.
finding_ledger.resolution: Ignored .specify/extensions/.cache/ and .specify/bugs/ while retaining official extension sources.

finding_ledger.finding: Spec Kit path overrides, traversal, or symlinks could redirect writes outside the repository.
finding_ledger.resolution: Added local path-boundary checks and focused negative controls.

finding_ledger.finding: Shell GitHub issue creation is an external side effect.
finding_ledger.resolution: The supported issue-write path is structured GitHub MCP with an explicit repository target and inherited target authorization. Quote-aware tokenization plus bounded static unwrapping for env, command, sudo, eval, bash/sh/zsh/dash/ksh, PowerShell, and cmd rejects reproduced direct, repository-flag, quoted executable-path, gh/gh.exe issue, and GitHub API write forms. Read-only gh issue list, view, status, help, explicit GET queries, documentation, search, test names, unrelated quoted executables, and local output remain allowed.

finding_ledger.finding: The first normalized phrase matcher blocked benign shell text containing issue create/new, workflow, or GitHub API examples.
finding_ledger.resolution: Replaced global phrase matching with quote-aware shell-segment, token, executable-position, namespace, and action recognition. Retained 29 benign/read-only controls and all prior malicious-form controls in the focused suite.

finding_ledger.finding: The earlier command-position matcher did not inspect static env, command, sudo, interpreter, eval, PowerShell, or cmd wrapper payloads and treated field-bearing explicit GET API calls as writes.
finding_ledger.resolution: Added bounded recursive static-wrapper extraction to depth 4 and made an explicit GitHub API method take precedence over field-induced POST inference; focused RED/GREEN coverage now includes malicious and benign wrapper controls.

finding_ledger.finding: Removing quotes before space-based tokenization allowed a quoted Windows or POSIX GitHub CLI executable path containing spaces to evade the issue-write guard.
finding_ledger.resolution: Added quote-aware tokenization that preserves a quoted executable as one token, plus direct, PowerShell call-operator, env, command, and shell-wrapper controls and unrelated-executable negative controls.

finding_ledger.finding: The earlier predicate denied all direct gh issue actions, including read-only list, view, status, and help.
finding_ledger.resolution: Classified the locally documented mutating actions explicitly, handled repository flags before namespace or action, and retained read-only action controls.

finding_ledger.finding: Generic or Codex Apps GitHub issue-write tools could bypass a shell-only guard.
finding_ledger.resolution: Extended matching to actual mcp__codex_apps__github_create_issue and generic GitHub issue-write names; added unauthorized and repository-mismatch tests.

finding_ledger.finding: An agent-authored constitution must not self-ratify.

The shell issue deny is defense in depth, not a complete interpreter or network capability sandbox. Wrapper recognition is deliberately bounded to the retained static forms and recursion depth 4; xargs/find execution, Python or custom launchers, fully dynamic construction, and alternative network clients remain UNVERIFIED. Only the structured MCP route is supported for Spec Kit issue creation.
